input.task: In the Travel category, find the cheapest book and tell me its exact price.

provenance: the first live-PLANNER case: no stub_plan, the plan must come from the real model, because the capability it grades — deriving 'cheapest' from a category with no sort control — is answer synthesis, which a hand-written plan would smuggle in. Ground truth hand-verified 2026-08-17 by an eval-side probe over all 11 Travel products: minimum price £23.21, 'The Road to Little Dribbling: Adventures of an American in Britain'. The sandbox's prices are frozen, so the label is stable. Graded on the price string with the book title as identity anchor — exact-matching a free-form title against a planner's phrasing would fail for the wrong reason. Tagged full only: it spends real LLM tokens and must never run in a gate.

triage.watched_red_twice: red for two honest reasons, in order: (1) eval_adapter.run_case has no dispatch for `planner: 'live'` — today it would execute an empty stub plan and fail INV-0-loud; the adapter extension is the first M6 implementation step and THIS case is its red driver. (2) once dispatched, the M5 held-out probe (2/8) predicts the planner itself fails multi-entity comparison — the one-hop-deep gap named in docs/analysis.md. Green requires closing both, which is what makes it an L3 worth having.
triage.cost_note: one page load + one or two planner calls per run, ~$0.01 at the M5 average; needs OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment (absent → the run must fail loudly, never stub itself: hard rule 4).
